caption: Residents commute across the Trishuli river on a newly installed zip wire in the aftermath of flash floods in Devighat.

Brasília, Brazil The Brazilian president, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, attends an Independence Day parade. The rightwing presidential hopeful Senator Flávio Bolsonaro is seeking to capitalise on a crisis engulfing the country’s supreme court, where two justices accuse each other of wrongdoing.

Coventry, UK The chancellor, John Healey, delivers a speech at the Manufacturing Technology Centre. In his first big address since taking up the job in July, Healey said boosting economic growth would be his priority and warned that Labour must be honest on spending.

Nuuk, Greenland Denmark’s prime minister, Mette Frederiksen, joins the European Commission president, Ursula von der Leyen, and Greenland’s head of government, Jens-Frederik Nielsen, on a visit to Eutelsat OneWeb, a company that provides broadband satellite internet services.

Portsmouth, UK A local resident collects some of the discarded life jackets near Eastney beach after unrest following the arrival of a boat carrying asylum seekers. Ministers condemned the ‘thuggish and intimidating behaviour’ of far-right activists who blocked roads in the city.

London, UK A journalist looks at a section of the Bayeux tapestry during a press preview at the British Museum. The 70-metre embroidery has returned to Britain for the first time in almost 1,000 years, on loan as part of an agreement between the UK and France.

Venice, Italy Pamela Anderson poses at the Hotel Excelsior Lido pier during the city’s film festival. Her latest movie, Place to Be, is been screening out of competition. She was honoured at a gala on Sunday evening for her work in the fight against Aids.

Prague, Czechia A gardener cuts a cluster of grapes in the south gardens of Prague Castle. More than 500kg of grapes are expected to be harvested from its 262 Hibernal vines to produce wine for the castle’s official needs. The harvest began two weeks earlier than usual because of a very hot summer.

Belgrade, Serbia People gather around the grave of the former Bosnian Serb army commander and war criminal Ratko Mladić at the Topcider cemetery. Mladić, 84, died last week while serving a life sentence for genocide and other crimes against humanity carried out during the Bosnian war.

Zaporizhzhia, Ukraine Rescuers work at the site of a Russian drone strike on a shopping centre. The City Center mall has been closed since the beginning of September because of persistent Russian attacks on civilian infrastructure. No casualties were reported after the strike.

Kathmandu, Nepal Children attend a gathering to observe a national day of mourning for victims of flash floods and mudslides triggered by a glacier collapse. At least 1,342 people were killed in Nepal, with a further 5,000 remaining missing across the region.

Bandar Abbas, Iran A boy stands with his bicycle on a beach overlooking commercial vessels anchored in the strait of Hormuz. On Sunday, the former US defence secretary Leon Panetta said the Iran conflict was likely to drag on for another six months and risked becoming another ‘forever war in the Middle East’.
New York, US Revellers take part in the J’ouvert celebration during the annual West Indian Day parade in Brooklyn.
Man with beard dressed in a fuchsia pink leather jacket wields a sword over a giant hand with a head appearing to scream towering over him in the background.

London, UK The Big London Tattoo show returns for its fifth year, showcasing the skills of more than 500 international tattoo artists at the ExCel centre. Competitions and a fire show feature among the weekend’s events.

Andøya, Norway The German startup Isar Aerospace launches its unmanned Spectrum rocket into orbit. Saturday’s launch from from the Andøya Spaceport marked a breakthrough for Europe, which wants to send satellites into space independently, reducing its reliance on the US amid the shifting global order.

Venice, Italy Noel Gallagher and Liam Gallagher attend the red carpet event for the screening of Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger at the Venice film festival. Directed by Dylan Southern and Will Lovelace, the documentary was shot during the band’s 2025 reunion tour.

San Diego, US Large waves generated by Hurricane Marie crash along the coastline at La Jolla’s Windansea beach. In recent days, the category 1 hurricane has been spinning around in the Pacific along with category 4 Hurricane Lowell and Tropical Storm Karina.

West Kalimantan, Indonesia Mother and baby orangutans are evacuated by officials owing to El Niño-fuelled wildfires fires in Ketapang district. Indonesian authorities are stepping up efforts to contain fires that are still burning across Sumatra and Kalimantan, with thick smog drifting to Malaysia, Singapore and the Philippines.
credit: Muffidz Masum/Indonesia Ministry of Forestry/YIARI/AFP/Getty Images

caption: Java, Indonesia A helicopter drops water on a fire at the Putri Cempo landfill in Solo, Central Java. The fire began Wednesday, with authorities battling to prevent it spreading further.

Montreux, Switzerland A fan poses next to a statue of Freddie Mercury festooned with flowers, messages and balloons on what would have been the Queen frontman’s 80th birthday. Mercury moved to the resort town in the late 1980s, staying until just a few weeks before his death in 1991.
Fujin City, China Tourists ride a sightseeing vehicle past a rice field painting at the 10,000-Mu Rice Park. The agricultural tourism complex is located in Jiamusi, Heilongjiang province.

Nuwakot, Nepal Members of the Nepali army use wooden sticks to search for survivors of deadly flash floods triggered by a glacial and rock collapse on 26 August. Ten days on, the authorities are still searching for thousands of missing people.
Nuwakot, Nepal Flash flood survivors rest inside a relief shelter. Survivors say they can no longer rebuild their homes after the landscape was violently transformed by the disaster.

Gaza City, Gaza Mourners gathered at the funeral of 100 people, whose bodies were retrieved from the ruins of destroyed residential buildings after Israeli airstrikes. Israel has killed more than 1,200 Palestinians in Gaza since agreeing to a ceasefire on 10 October 2025, according to the territory’s health ministry.
Hutubi, China A combine harvester unloads corn kernels into a truck in the Xinjiang region of north-west China. Local farmers use corn drying technology to aid the autumn harvest.

San Diego, US A cosplayer dressed as Garrett ‘The Garbageman’ Garrison, the larger-than-life character played by Jason Momoa in last year’s A Minecraft Movie, during the first day of Anime San Diego 2026 at the city’s convention centre.

Ingwavuma, South Africa Zulu women gather outside the royal palace in the south-east Kwazulu-Natal province during the annual uMkhosi woMhlanga ceremony. The annual event in which thousands of young women present tall reeds to their monarch in a traditional rite of womanhood.

London, UK Debutantes attend the Queen Charlotte’s 247th anniversary ball at One Whitehall Place. King George III introduced the event in 1780 to celebrate his wife’s birthday, with young, wealthy women – known as ‘debs’ - traditionally presented to the king or queen.

Birmingham, UK Delegates arrive at the annual Reform UK conference, which took place amid scrutiny over the party’s finances. Party officials were recently filmed in an undercover investigation appearing to plot a way of dodging electoral laws on foreign donations.
In Kyiv's Bucha district, two people walk through smoky rubble after a Russian strike.

Devighat, Nepal Women view the widened channel of the Trishuli River after flash floods in Devighat. Rescuers have built temporary bridges to reach remote areas and dug through the ruins of hydropower projects in the Himalayas to rescue hundreds of trapped workers, as the death toll passed 1,000 nearly ⁠a week after devastating ​floods left a trail of destruction across the country’s towns and valleys.

Rasuwa, Nepal Members of a search and rescue team at the Trishuli-3A hydropower project in Rasuwa rescue a man. Two people were pulled out alive from the hydropower tunnel nine days after deadly flash floods buried the project in deep mud and left them trapped.

Kathmandu, Nepal Relatives mourn during the symbolic cremation of four members of the Magar family who remain missing after the flash floods , at Pashupatinath Temple in Kathmandu. The bodies of some of those killed in the Nepal-Tibet flood disaster may never be found, and some of those who are found may never be identified, a renowned forensic scientist, Prof Richard Bassed, said this week.

Devighat, Nepal Rescue workers inspect damaged structures after the recent flash flooding along the Trishuli River in Devighat. The disaster was triggered by a glacier collapse that sent a deluge of ice, rock and mud through Nepal’s border region with China.

Galchi, Nepal A mark shows the mud level on a wall in a classroom at Bageshwori secondary school after flash floods in Galchi. The Himalayas – spanning Nepal, India, China, Bhutan and Pakistan – are warming twice as fast as the global average, putting the region at increased risk of avalanches , landslides and floods.
Kyiv, Ukraine Children play with bubbles during traditional back-to-school celebrations in Kyiv.

Kyiv, Ukraine People visit a McDonald’s restaurant that was the first to open in Ukraine, in an area hit by ​​numerous Russian missile attacks. Volodymyr Zelenskyy this week declared that Russia’s airspace was becoming unsafe for commercial airlines, as Vladimir Putin promised to increase strikes against Ukraine’s energy facilities in the run-up to winter.
Al-Mansouri, Lebanon Smoke billows from houses hit during Israeli attacks in the town of al-Mansouri in southern Lebanon.

Sinjil, West Bank A Palestinian man scans a valley with a flashlight during a volunteer nightwatch to help prevent Israeli settler attacks in the town of Sinjil. Israelis shot dead two teenagers in the Palestinian village of al-Mughayyir and Israeli troops razed the village of Khirbet al-Taban, outside Hebron, in the latest attacks across the occupied West Bank.

Gaza Palestinian children watch a film screening organised by the Little Wings Cinema initiative in Gaza. Israel’s far-right national security minister, Itamar Ben-Gvir, set out a plan this week for the illegal forced expulsion of all Palestinians from the Gaza Strip, with the intention of sending them abroad. Earlier this year, an independent UN inquiry found that Israel continued to commit genocide by deliberately targeting Palestinian children in Gaza.
Big Sur, California Sage Harvey throws a rope off the roof of his house as the Plaskett Fire approaches.

Pattaya, Thailand A crew member walks on the flight deck of the nuclear-powered aircraft carrier USS Abraham Lincoln as it heads towards Laem Chabang port. The aircraft carrier has been plagued by reports of deteriorating living conditions and poor mental health onboard , including attempted suicides, making headlines around the world and provoking criticism of Donald Trump’s war against Iran.

Menab, Iran A child receives treatment at a hospital in Menab after being wounded, according to Tasnim news agency, in a strike on a home where a wedding was being held in the city of Kuhestak. Iran accused the US of a war crime after a missile blast killed at least four people and injured 68 who were attending the wedding.
Port-au-Prince, Haiti A woman, overwhelmed with grief, is carried out of a funeral service for more than 20 people killed by armed gangs last week in Kenscoff, a neighbourhood near Port-au-Prince.

Washington DC, US A demonstrator dressed as a blood-covered Lady Justice attends a Defend the Vote rally at the Lincoln Memorial. A new system to screen millions of mail-in ballots for this November’s US midterm elections was thrown together so hastily, and tested so little, that a single scanning glitch could lead to entire batches of ballots being turned away, a whistleblower has told Congress.
London, England Costumed participants in the Notting Hill carnival travel on the tube.
Basra, Iraq A man dives into the Shatt al-Arab River amid soaring temperatures in Basra.

Lake Baringo, Kenya A person holds a Nile crocodile at Lake Baringo, where Kenya Wildlife Service is facilitating the capture and translocation of the animals to reduce cases of human-wildlife conflict near Marigat.

International Space Station The European Space Agency astronaut Sophie Adenot works during a spacewalk outside the ISS. Adenot and the Nasa astronaut Anil Menon completed the installation and activation of a spare space-to-ground antenna.
